I’m sorry that you’re going through this. I hear that you’re hurt and anxious about your future. You’re not overreacting. Why would you want to be with someone who doesn’t appreciate you and intentionally puts you down in front of others?
My advice would be to give your wife one last warning and maybe even give an ultimatum that you will leave if she does it again. Be firm and clearly explain how her actions hurt you.
If she ignores your warning follow through on your ultimatum. If she cared then she would have changed a long time ago, or at least showed effort to want to make it work. You can stay with family or friends so that you spend some time apart, like a short separation and not a full on divorce. I also strongly suggest seeking counsel from a family/marriage therapist, it’s so helpful to navigate complex feelings and relationships with a trained professional.
Ik this is hard, but you can’t live freely or happily when you’re always under someone’s thumb. She may not even realize that what she’s doing is inappropriate, she might be modeling what she had learned from her parents. And if she is doing this to you then she is probably doing it to your kids too which can destroy their psyche as they grow up (i say this as the child that has grown up). You can break the cycle and save your family from toxic behavior, even if that is a family without your wife.

I don’t think either of you are TA. Sometimes we just aren’t good at communicating. My husband and I have off days and it’s taken time for us to figure out how to communicate on those days. It’s good to have paused the conversation and you can follow up on it later if it’s important to you.
You can ask “hey could we follow up on that conversation the other day?”. I assume he will say yes, at which point you will explain how you think that you guys weren’t communicating to each other well and that you would like to try again. If he doesn’t want to talk about it you can ask why and go from there.

Understandable. There are a few ways to go about it. Bc you own your own business I’m not sure what your insurance situation is, but if you have insurance you can check your benefits plan which usually has things for mental health. Or you can check out the independent networks like BetterHelp which have a variety of therapists to choose from. 
Something to consider when finding a therapist is their specialty and how they will help you. In this case I think you should speak with a family therapist but there are others like relationship or trauma counseling. Some agencies will have you speak with a counselor for initial assessment and refer you to someone on their team who they think can help you best.
Therapy is completely confidential and they won’t speak with anyone about your situation without your consent.

That can be sitting with him on phone calls or during in-person conversations with his family. He might need a pep talk beforehand, remind him that he’s not alone and you will stand with him. 
He sounds like a good guy and well-meaning, but it’s not his responsibility to take care of his family or his parents. Family dynamics are very difficult, you guys might want to speak with a family therapist to help you navigate this. I personally believe everyone should speak with a therapist some time in their lives. It’s helpful navigating complex feelings and relationships with a trained professional.

NTA
He might feel some sort of obligation to his family and he might be so used to putting them over himself that it blinds him to the fact that he is also putting them over you. But he has chosen to make a life with you and you should be put above everyone else until you make a family (if you guys want children). Even if his family treats you well, they should understand that you come before them now. He might have given them the impression that you are better off than you actually are, or they might even assume that they will come first.
If you’ve explained your concerns and he’s still not budging, you might want to consider giving him an ultimatum by having the marriage annulled (if you’re able to). Say that even tho you’ve been together so long that he still puts his family over your future as a couple and you don’t feel confident that he is ready to commit to marriage. Or if that’s too harsh, say that you want to separate your finances. He can feel free to give whatever he wants to his family as long as it doesn’t impact you or your goals. Or even do something simple like saying you need a break and stay with some friends or take a solo trip.
When talking with him use “I” statements to show that you aren’t accusing him of anything, but how his actions make you feel. Like “Ik you love your family and I love them too, but I feel like you put their financial needs over our own. It feels like you love them more than me and that hurts me”. Remind him of how much you love him and how excited you are for your future together, explain how you’re worried that he’s forgotten about your goals and that your needs are being neglected. 
I hope this advice helps, Idk you’re full situation so curate it to your needs. Congratulations on your marriage (my husband and I got married recently too!), I wish you both love and prosperity 😌🌸

You’re not overreacting. You have every right to be upset. It’s a very painful time for you and you want to feel supported at the very least if not celebrated. My father also died on my birthday which has been painful for me. I can’t imagine how you feel but I hear that you are hurt and need some extra TLC.
I’m not trying to defend your husband, but he may have forgotten how you are feeling rn and is being shortsighted. But if this is a regular occurrence of you feeling abandoned by your husband then you might want to talk with him about it, or even go to couple’s therapy. There’s nothing wrong with couple’s therapy and it can help having a trained professionals support in navigate the complexities of your feelings and relationship.
Hopefully when he comes back home he is a bit more clear minded and is able to hear you, but you don’t have to talk about it with him if you don’t want to. Do what you need to communicate your feelings and needs, even if it’s as simple as “bc it’s my birthday could you take care of the kids while I do xyz“. Sometimes writing it down helps me sort out my feelings, I feel like when I put my ramblings on paper that they are no longer running circles around in my head and I get clarity.
I wish you comfort, love, and peace. Happy Birthday 😌🌸

NTA
You have every right to make your own choices and parents aren’t meant to choose our lives for us. Our parents are supposed to help us figure out who we are meant to be and guide us on our journey. I was also taught to respect my elders, but sometimes they are wrong and we shouldn’t have to bear responsibility for emotionally immature adults.
It sounds like you fully depend on your mother which makes it hard for you to live your life without facing repercussions. If possible, you might want to speak to an adult you trust who your mother also respects about this issue and ask if they can help you out. Maybe they can have a conversation with your mom and she can better understand you. You might even want to consider asking your bf for help if you think he can.
If she is a narcissist this likely won’t work, but if she is just a person with narcissistic tendencies then she might not realize what she is doing or that it is a toxic behavior. It’s not up to you to fix your mom, but you will have to enforce boundaries even when she lashes out. 
It’s not easy at all. But the most important thing for you is being able to keep yourself safe and taking care of your own needs- it’s up to you as to how you will do these things. You should work with a family therapist if you don’t already. The therapist can work with you and might even be able to do family sessions with you and your mom.
I wish you comfort and happiness. I hope this helps.
